shadows.name: shadow-sm

shadows.name: focus-halo

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: State changes: hover, colour, opacity, switch track (120-150ms).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Arrivals: dialogs and notifications 160ms, band 180ms, stamped notice 220ms, filter input width 200ms, switch thumb 150ms.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Hover and state transitions on rows, chips, buttons and tools.

motion.name: stamp-in
motion.value: 320ms ease-out; 0% opacity 0, scale(1.12) rotate(-2deg); 55% opacity 1, scale(.98) rotate(.4deg); 100% none
motion.purpose: The one authored motion moment: the ticket landing in the band (stamp-again replays it on a second click) and the check icon in the bottom notice.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce): transitions 0.01ms; band, ticket stamp, notice icon, dialogs, notices, preview fade-in 120ms; busy pulses stop at opacity .6; preview spinner slows to 2.4s
motion.purpose: Nothing travels or scales; feedback stays visible.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Band stacks (ticket and close, then Download again), commands wrap, stamped notice spans the width.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Tree hidden, operator site name hidden (wordmark stays), archive action icon-only, settings drawer overlays, admin tabs scroll under a fade mask.

breakpoints.name: tiny
breakpoints.purpose: Brand only: the wordmark hides, the mark alone carries the brand.

breakpoints.name: no-hover
breakpoints.purpose: Checkboxes and download chips always visible.

narrative.overview:
A well-lit counter in a dark archive. The room is quiet and familiar: a top bar, a breadcrumb, a full-width details table with name, modified date and size, the shape every visitor already knows from a file manager. The light falls on one place only, the counter where a file is handed over. Every file states its size plainly in a chip at the end of its row; clicking a name unfolds the row in place into a band that says "Download 7.5 GB" on the one gradient button in the interface, with the direct link, curl and wget beneath it; once a download starts, a ticket is stamped right where the button was, saying when it started, how big it is, and that it is resumable, and the button steps back to a quiet "Download again". Downloads started anywhere else get the same ticket as a receipt at the bottom of the screen.

This is an Operate surface. Density is product-UI density: a 14px body, 36px rows and controls (44px on touch), a 4px spacing grid, hairline borders between tinted near-black planes. The brand lives in precise details rather than spectacle: the h6ai hexagon and wordmark in the top bar, one reserved accent colour per skin that marks only the download and selection path, and the blue-to-violet gradient that belongs to the logo and the Download button. Everything else is neutral and recedes.

The system is dark only, shipped as five generated, AA-checked skins (Midnight by default, Graphite, Deep Sea, Ember, OLED Black). It uses the platform's system font stack and loads no web fonts. Icons are inline stroke SVG that follow the text colour. Nothing is decorative: no gradient text, no eyebrow labels, no coloured side stripes, no glyph icons.
keyCharacteristics: Familiar file-manager structure; the brand shows up in the download path, not in ornament.
Tinted near-black planes separated by 1px hairlines; depth by tone first, shadow second.
One reserved accent per skin, spent only on download and selection.
One gradient, on the primary Download button and in the logo.
System fonts, tabular numerals, 14px body, 36px minimum targets (44px on coarse pointers).
Five dark skins with identical structure; colours are swapped wholesale via the skin attribute.
Every started download is stamped with a ticket: accent stub, dashed perforation, what and how big.

rules.name: The Reserved Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent and its soft wash mark only the download and selection path: the size-labelled download chip, the band's Download button, the archive "Download N items" action, the stamped ticket in the band and in the notice, selected rows with their checkboxes, and the admin's representations of downloads (the "download" level chip, file and archive download events, the theme-preview miniatures). If a new element is not a download, an archive download, or a selection, it does not get the accent; no skin may reuse its accent hue for links.

rules.name: The One Gradient Rule
rules.body: The brand gradient appears in exactly two places: the primary Download button, which wears the skin's accent gradient, and the logo, which keeps the fixed azure to violet in every skin. The admin theme previews may draw both in miniature. No gradient backgrounds, borders, dividers or text anywhere else; once a download has started, the button gives up the gradient.

rules.name: The Link-and-Focus Rule
rules.body: Cornflower Link is the colour of links, focus rings and the caret, and of "this setting is on". It never marks a download.

rules.name: The Second Voice Rule
rules.body: Primary buttons outside the download path (log in, save, add, check) fill with Cornflower Action. A violet or gradient Save button is a bug.

rules.name: The Dark Only Rule
rules.body: Every surface is dark. New skins are new dark palettes on the same tokens, generated and checked for 4.5:1 text and accent contrast on every plane and 3:1 for input borders. There is no light mode.

rules.name: The System Stack Rule
rules.body: No web fonts. Type comes from the system UI and monospace stacks; the strict CSP and the "fast on any device" promise both depend on it.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Numerals are tabular everywhere, so sizes, dates, counts and ticket times line up down a column.

rules.name: The Four Thresholds Rule
rules.body: Responsive changes happen at 560px, 720px, 1080px and on pointer: coarse (plus hover: none for always-visible affordances). The single exception is 360px, reserved for the brand: below it the wordmark gives way to the mark. Do not add new breakpoints for a single component.

rules.name: The Target Rule
rules.body: Nothing interactive is smaller than 36px, or 44px on a coarse pointer.

rules.name: The Raised Path Rule
rules.body: Only the download path is lifted inside the page flow. Cards, tiles and rows stay flat.

rules.name: The Still Motion Rule
rules.body: Under reduced motion nothing travels or scales: the band, the ticket stamp, dialogs, notices and preview simply fade in 120ms, busy pulses stop at 60% opacity, and only the preview spinner keeps turning, slowly.

rules.name: The No Decoration Rule
rules.body: No gradient text, no eyebrow or kicker labels above headings, no coloured side-stripe borders, no glyph or emoji icons. Every UI icon is an inline 24-unit stroke SVG with 2px round strokes in currentColor from the shared icon set.

rules.name: The Receipt Rule
rules.body: Every download that starts gets exactly one stamped ticket, in the band when it started there and as the bottom notice otherwise: what started, how big, and whether it resumes.

dos: **Do** give every file row a size-labelled download chip, and label the Download button with the size ("Download 7.5 GB").
**Do** stamp a started download with the ticket form (accent stub, dashed accent perforation, tabular metadata) and demote the button to "Download again".
**Do** spend the accent only on the download and selection path, and Cornflower only on links, focus, primary non-download actions and "on" states.
**Do** keep new screens on the three tonal planes with 1px hairlines; lift only the band and the Download button, float only overlays.
**Do** use the 4px spacing scale and the 6/10/14px radii, and keep every target at 36px (44px on coarse pointers).
**Do** take colours from the skin tokens so a new component works in all five dark skins unchanged.
**Do** use the system font stacks with tabular numerals, and cap prose and help text at 72ch.
**Do** honour reduced motion: fade, don't travel.
donts: **Don't** put the accent or its wash on anything that is not a download, an archive download or a selection.
**Don't** use the brand gradient anywhere except the primary Download button and the logo; never on text, borders or backgrounds.
**Don't** add a light theme or light surfaces.
**Don't** add eyebrow or kicker labels above headings, coloured side-stripe borders, gradient text, or glyph and emoji icons.
**Don't** introduce breakpoints beyond 560px, 720px, 1080px and pointer: coarse.
**Don't** give cards, tiles or rows a resting shadow.
**Don't** add another rotating, overshooting or stamping animation; the ticket stamp is the only one.
